name: Jellyfin to Jellyfin
description: Mirrors remote Jellyfin libraries into local .strm trees and proxies playback, without downloading media.
overview: Point this plugin at one or more remote Jellyfin servers and it writes .strm/.nfo files plus artwork into a path your own server can index, then streams the original file through the local server so your users can browse and play remote content from your own libraries.

versions.changelog: Mapping table fix. The per-row On checkbox was created as a Jellyfin checkbox (is=emby-checkbox) without the label/span wrapper that element requires: it threw while initialising, so the first row showed a black box that ignored clicks and the rest of the table was left half-styled. Rows now use plain checkbox, select, input and button controls, which toggle and render the same in every browser and keep the compact grid layout. Nothing else changed, so 0.3.1.0 configurations, mappings and mirrors keep working as they are.

Mapping table redesign. Load remote libraries now fills one row per remote library (id, name and type come from the catalog), so nothing has to be typed from memory. Reloading matches rows by remote item id first and by name second, keeps the on/off state, folder and target of the rows you already configured, adds new libraries as Off, and keeps mappings whose remote library disappeared at the end instead of dropping them. The target column is now a 'Merge with local library' dropdown of the local libraries plus a trailing 'Create new library' entry with an optional name box (blank = remote library name); an existing library is attached by id, as the local-libraries endpoint now returns the library itemId. Folder name and Type show the defaults that will be used as 'Auto: <library>' and 'Auto: <type>' placeholders, and update live when the remote library of a row changes.

Log in with a remote user instead of an API key. Jellyfin API keys are server-wide and always administrator level; the plugin now authenticates as a regular user (POST /Users/AuthenticateByName), caches the session token in memory, retries on 401 and discovers libraries through GET /UserViews. The password is never written to .strm files and no secret travels in a URL anymore: /api/test and /api/libraries are POST with a JSON body. Breaking: the per-instance ApiKey setting is gone - configure a user name and password instead (a non-admin account that sees the libraries you mirror is enough). The mirror now only contains items that account can actually play, so dead database entries no longer produce .strm files that answer 404.

Removed-item cleanup: new per-instance 'Remove stale .strm/.nfo files' option deletes mirror files whose source item is gone (and prunes the folders left empty) after a successful sync, and the report shows 'staleRemoved'. The pass never runs when a listing is empty or an item failed, and it only touches generated .strm/.nfo files plus artwork when artwork download is enabled.
